- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) or volatile, model often underestimates or fails to anticipate sharp drops; increase forecast marginally to account for downside risk.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days), leading to overshoot; apply smoothing or lag correction for the next 3-5 periods.
- In low-sentiment environments, mean reversion is stronger; forecast should trend toward historical mean (last 10-15 days) rather than extrapolating upward.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative within 3-5 days, model often fails to adjust; apply a downward bias of 1-2% for the next 5 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the forecast window (first 5-7 days) — reduce initial values by 0.5–1.5% to align with true behavior.
- When sentiment is high but price is flat or declining, model may misread sentiment as bullish — reduce forecast slope or add downward adjustment.
